I couldn't find a series bible or reference files in the working directory, so I made these assumptions:

- **How it's made:** text-to-video in the Dreamina/Jimeng-style Seedance interface, with the model's own sound turned on. Seedance 2.x can generate sound with the picture. The setting names below are the usual ones. Your UI may label them a little differently.
- **The song:** the prompt doesn't name a real Armenian song. It asks for an era-appropriate *style* (Soviet Armenian pop with synths, as heard on the radio) with unclear vocals. A named song would be a rights problem, and the model would garble the lyrics anyway. If you have a licensed track, add it in the edit and lower the generated music.
- **The look:** a Soviet-era Yerevan courtyard built of pink-and-apricot tuff stone, with wooden balconies and a grapevine trellis. It's filmed like 35mm film stock of the period. There's no on-screen text, because the series title belongs in the edit.
- **The girl:** she wears ordinary, modest everyday clothes and is shown naturally, with no glamour styling.

## FINAL

**UI settings**
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | Seedance 2.5 (use Pro / the highest quality tier if there's a choice) |
| Mode | Text-to-Video |
| Aspect ratio | 9:16 (vertical) |
| Duration | 10 s |
| Resolution | 1080p |
| Frame rate | 24 fps (if offered) |
| Audio | On (generate sound) |
| Camera control | Push-in / Dolly in, slow (if there's a camera preset; otherwise the prompt covers it) |
| Seed | Fixed (write it down once you get a take you like, so you can match it later) |
| Negative prompt (if there's a field) | text, subtitles, captions, logos, watermark, modern cars, satellite dishes, plastic windows, air conditioners, smartphones, neon, modern clothing, distorted hands, extra fingers, warped clothespins, flicker, fast camera movement, cuts |

**Prompt (copy-ready)**
```
Vertical 9:16 single continuous shot, 10 seconds, no cuts. Summer evening, 1984, an old residential courtyard in Yerevan, Soviet Armenia. Four-storey buildings of pink and apricot volcanic tuff stone, wooden balconies with peeling turquoise paint, a grapevine trellis over part of the yard, a mulberry tree, a dusty beige Zhiguli parked by the wall, distant children's voices.

A 16-year-old Armenian girl with a long dark braid, wearing a faded floral cotton sundress and simple sandals, hangs white bedsheets and a few small cotton garments on a clothesline strung across the courtyard. She takes wooden clothespins from a tin basin at her hip, shakes out a damp sheet with a soft snap, and pins it to the line, unhurried and absorbed. A light breeze lifts the sheet; warm sunlight glows through the fabric. Near the end she pauses, tilts her head toward the music, and a faint, private smile appears.

On a ground-floor windowsill nearby, a neighbour's old Soviet radio plays a 1980s Armenian estrada pop song: warm synthesizer, bass guitar, light drum machine, a female vocal with indistinct lyrics, slightly tinny AM sound echoing off the stone walls.

Camera: starts as a medium-wide shot from courtyard level with the radio soft in the foreground edge, then makes one slow, steady push-in toward the girl, ending in a medium close-up of her face and hands framed by the glowing sheet. Smooth dolly movement, no shake, no zoom jumps.

Light: golden-hour late sun, low and warm, long soft shadows, amber backlight and rim light on her hair and the sheets, dust motes in the air, deep warm shadows in the archways.

Look: 1980s Soviet 35mm colour film, Kodak/Svema-like warm palette, gentle grain, slight halation on highlights, natural skin texture, nostalgic, quiet, cinematic realism.

Sound: the radio song as the main layer, wooden clothespin clicks, fabric flutter, swallows chirping, faint children and a distant tram bell. No dialogue.

No on-screen text, no subtitles, no modern objects.
```
